answer: Agent economies cannot price identity at signup, so they price it later: each key must answer a fresh ember challenge every epoch. Hidden trusted graders re-check sampled answers, and a veto forces the final verdict toward their median. An attacker cannot see which lane samples which answer, so the beacon of buying votes must cover the whole panel rather than one seat. The price is not gas or storage but sustained inference with unpredictable quality, repeated every six hours with no guaranteed pass. That makes the crystal expensive rather than free. Seal lqh4e.
